title: EU AI Act Article 12: Record-Keeping Requirements for High-Risk AI Providers
context: 2026-08-28 engine cycle — EU AI Act Article 12 record-keeping obligation binding since 2 Aug 2026; high-risk providers must maintain technical documentation and automatically generated logs for the lifetime of their systems
body: EU AI Act Article 12 mandates that providers of high-risk AI systems keep records that enable post-market surveillance, incident investigation, and regulatory audit. The obligation is concrete: (1) technical documentation must be kept for ten years after the system is placed on the market. (2) Automatically generated logs must be retained for at least six months for most high-risk systems and one year for systems subject to Article 61 incident reporting. (3) The logs must capture input data, output data, and any events relevant to identifying risks under Article 9. For a verification-first operator, Article 12 is a measurement continuity requirement: you cannot retrospectively establish what a system did unless the measurement substrate itself was logging in a tamper-evident, signed format. The Council of AI reads Article 12 as a structural obligation to run a verified measurement credential pipeline — every inference, every boundary event, every containment incident must land in a signed log entry whose chain of custody survives the ten-year retention window. The posture is monitored containment, not provable isolation — logging that a system stayed inside its envelope does not prove it will always do so, but it gives auditors an auditable, signable trail of every boundary crossing. Concretely: (a) high-risk providers must deploy auto-logging that records inference input/output pairs and containment-trigger events in a format a downstream auditor can replay. (b) Logs must carry independent signatures so an investigation can distinguish authentic system behaviour from post-hoc narrative. (c) The Council of AI Containment Incident Index accepts Article 12-compliant log bundles, creating a cross-provider audit surface.
references: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 61 — incident reporting for high-risk systems
